title: Skipping check_array with validate_data(skip_check_array=True) also skips the finite check, so add it back explicitly
answers: SelectKBest transform accepts inf with set_output(transform='pandas')
why does transform not reject NaN/inf when the input is a DataFrame?
feature selector pandas output skips validation
body:
Symptom: with `set_output(transform="pandas")` and a DataFrame input, feature selectors like SelectKBest let inf (and NaN) through `transform`. The same input as a numpy array raises "Input X contains infinity/NaN".
Root cause: sklearn/feature_selection/_base.py:SelectorMixin.transform keeps the DataFrame as-is (`preserve_X`) by passing `skip_check_array=preserve_X` to `validate_data`. That skips check_array completely, so `ensure_all_finite` has no effect.
Fix pattern: after `validate_data(..., skip_check_array=True)`, call `assert_all_finite(X, input_name="X")` (from sklearn.utils.validation) yourself when the estimator does not allow NaN. Read the `get_tags(self).input_tags.allow_nan` tag once and use it for both checks.
Constraints: allow_nan=True turns off the whole finite check on both the numpy and the pandas paths, so inf passes too (VarianceThreshold, the only built-in selector that allows NaN, passes NaN and inf). Any other transformer that uses skip_check_array to keep the container type needs the same explicit check. SelectorMixin is a public mixin, so read tags with get_tags rather than __sklearn_tags__.
applies: sklearn/feature_selection SelectorMixin and any estimator that calls validate_data with skip_check_array=True
